findings: B original Go default1460 (true TUN1389) vs A/A-prime explicit1160 (true TUN1089), same exact binary/real underlay1500: receiver goodput +23.74%, client CPU/effective GiB -18.95%, server CPU/effective GiB -16.21%, source packets/effective GiB -25.08%. This is existing product configuration packet-size efficiency, NOT a new product code gain.
Absolute CPU seconds did NOT decrease client 31.02/31.17/31.15, server 28.73/29.66/28.50. It delivers more bytes at similar or greater near-full CPU, not new free CPU headroom.

B TCP forward app observed p99 626.8ms while server app processing p99 0.45ms. Small TCP TCP_INFO retrans segments37/43/36 and RTO p95 ~204/205/203ms; not first lost app seq proof.

limitations: One ARM VM source locked A/B/A-prime; A/A-prime small P99 drift 221 vs617ms, so do not assign stable causal P99 regression to B from this one run. Real small-source refusal B did not improve.

No physical WAN, x86 second-ISA B replication, default1460 GE1%, Windows, 3-second uplink failover, long P99 SLA or full no-HOL proof.
Cannot claim original Go-only versus whole Go+Rust optimization without matched before/after builds.
